balanceSheet.title: Balance sheet
balanceSheet.content:
Shareholders' equity is assets less liabilities; plotted against total liabilities to show leverage.

For Iluka Resources Limited: equity that grows only through revaluations or share issues is not the same as retained earnings.

What to watch:

  • Liabilities growing faster than equity
  • Goodwill share of equity after acquisitions

cashDebt.title: Cash and debt
cashDebt.content:
Cash & equivalents against total borrowings (leases excluded unless noted).

For Iluka Resources Limited: the DCF's net-debt bridge uses these balances at the latest balance-sheet date.

What to watch:

  • Net debt trend versus EBITDA
  • Refinancing dates and covenants in the filings

ebitda.title: EBITDA
ebitda.content:
EBITDA is earnings before interest, tax, depreciation and amortisation -- an operating-cash proxy that ignores capital intensity.

For Iluka Resources Limited: read it beside CapEx: a business that must reinvest most of its EBITDA is not as cash-generative as the margin suggests.

What to watch:

  • EBITDA margin trend
  • Gap between EBITDA and operating cash flow (working capital)

epsDps.title: EPS and dividends
epsDps.content:
EPS is net income per share; DPS is the cash dividend paid per share. Both are in major currency units.

For Iluka Resources Limited: the payout ratio (DPS / EPS) shows how much of earnings is returned versus reinvested.

What to watch:

  • EPS growth versus net income growth (dilution)
  • Dividends funded from earnings, not debt

fcf.title: Free cash flow
fcf.content:
Reported FCF is operating cash flow less capital expenditure. Owner FCF (from the DCF) further deducts stock-based compensation, interest income and lease principal -- the cash an owner could actually take out.

For Iluka Resources Limited: the gap between net income and owner FCF is the earnings-quality question the valuation is built on.

What to watch:

  • FCF persistently below net income
  • Working-capital swings inflating one year's FCF

margins.title: Margins
margins.content:
Gross margin is revenue less cost of revenue; operating margin deducts operating expenses; net margin is after interest and tax.

For Iluka Resources Limited: the spread between gross and operating margin is the cost of running the business; a widening spread with flat gross margin means opex is growing faster than sales.

What to watch:

  • Direction of operating margin over several years, not one
  • One-offs (impairments, disposals) that distort net margin

ocfCapex.title: Operating cash flow and CapEx
ocfCapex.content:
Operating cash flow is cash generated by operations; CapEx is cash invested in fixed and intangible assets.

For Iluka Resources Limited: CapEx here is shown as stored (sign convention varies by ticker); the DCF splits it into stay-in-business and growth where disclosed.

What to watch:

  • CapEx rising faster than revenue
  • OCF that diverges from EBITDA

productionByProduct.title: Production volumes by product
productionByProduct.content:
Tonnes of each mineral sands product mined and processed in the period: zircon, rutile, synthetic rutile (ilmenite upgraded in Iluka's own SR kilns) and ilmenite (the lowest-value, highest-volume byproduct).

For Iluka Resources Limited: production depends on which ore bodies are being mined (Jacinth-Ambrosia for zircon-rich ore, Cataby/Narngulu for rutile) and on planned maintenance shuts, so a year-on-year drop is not automatically a demand problem.

What to watch:

  • Rutile and synthetic rutile production falling well below zircon-equivalent capacity after 2022 (mine sequencing, not demand)
  • Ilmenite sales far below production -- it is stockpiled when prices are weak

salesByProduct.title: Sales volumes by product
salesByProduct.content:
Tonnes of each product actually sold, which can diverge sharply from production when Iluka chooses to stockpile rather than sell into a weak price.

For Iluka Resources Limited: ilmenite sales fell from ~300kt (FY2015) to ~51kt (FY2025) even as production stayed well above that -- Iluka is deliberately withholding the lowest-margin product rather than selling it at a loss.

What to watch:

  • Sales consistently below production (rising stockpiles, a pricing call)
  • Sales spikes that draw down stockpiles rather than reflect current output

realizedPrices.title: Realised prices by product
realizedPrices.content:
The USD/tonne price Iluka actually realised for each product, benchmarked against the global mineral sands market. Zircon (premium) is the higher-grade ceramic-glaze grade; zircon (all products) blends in lower-grade zirconium chemical-feedstock sales. The AUD/USD rate (right axis) is shown because Iluka reports in AUD but prices are set in USD.

For Iluka Resources Limited: rutile and zircon prices peaked around FY2022-2023 (critical-minerals demand, supply tightness) and have since eased; a weaker AUD cushions AUD-reported revenue when USD prices fall.

What to watch:

  • Price trend versus China/EV-linked rare earths and titanium feedstock demand
  • Zircon premium-vs-all-products spread narrowing (grade mix)

zrsrUnitEconomics.title: ZRSR unit economics
zrsrUnitEconomics.content:
The margin per tonne on Iluka's three premium products (zircon, rutile, synthetic rutile -- excludes ilmenite): revenue per tonne against unit COGS and unit cash cost, all in A$/t.

For Iluka Resources Limited: unit cash cost nearly doubled from ~A$373/t (FY2016) to over A$1,000/t (FY2023-2025) on cost inflation and lower production volumes spreading fixed costs over fewer tonnes -- the spread to revenue per tonne is the real margin signal, not the EBITDA margin alone.

What to watch:

  • The gap between revenue per tonne and unit cash cost narrowing (margin compression)
  • Unit COGS rising faster than unit cash cost (depreciation of a large capital program, e.g. Eneabba)

mineralSandsEbitda.title: Mineral Sands segment EBITDA vs Group EBITDA
mineralSandsEbitda.content:
EBITDA of the core mineral sands mining and processing segment, against total group EBITDA.

For Iluka Resources Limited: the gap between the two lines is Iluka's rare earths growth bet -- the Eneabba refinery and related development spend sit outside Mineral Sands and currently a drag, not a contributor, on group EBITDA.

What to watch:

  • Group EBITDA falling further below Mineral Sands EBITDA as the refinery ramps costs ahead of revenue
  • Mineral Sands EBITDA margin trend in isolation from the rare earths build-out

profit.title: Profit lines
profit.content:
Gross profit is revenue less cost of revenue; operating income deducts operating expenses; net income is after interest, tax and one-offs.

For Iluka Resources Limited: the three lines together show where margin is made and lost between the top line and the bottom.

What to watch:

  • Operating income growing slower than gross profit (opex creep)
  • Net income far from operating income (interest, tax, one-offs)

revenue.title: Revenue
revenue.content:
Revenue is the top line: what customers paid for goods and services in the period, before any costs.

For Iluka Resources Limited: the growth rate matters more than the level; compare it with the DCF's base-case growth path below.

What to watch:

  • Acceleration or deceleration in YoY growth
  • Whether growth is organic or acquired
  • Interim rows show seasonality

sbc.title: Stock-based compensation and share count
sbc.content:
Stock-based comp is the expense of equity awards; shares outstanding shows the dilution it causes net of buybacks.

For Iluka Resources Limited: the DCF charges SBC as a cash cost and holds the share count flat, so this chart is the check on that assumption.

What to watch:

  • Share count rising while buybacks are advertised
  • SBC as a percentage of revenue
